In a thick forest, wherever you look, your eyes land on a tree.
Picture space that way: endless, and full of stars.
Every line of sight would end on a star, and the whole sky would blaze.
But the sky is dark. And it isn't dust, which would heat up and glow too.
In 1848, the poet Edgar Allan Poe guessed why: some starlight hasn't reached us yet.
He was mostly right. The universe isn't infinitely old, so starlight has had only about thirteen point eight billion years to travel.
So the dark between the stars is a clue that the universe had a beginning.
Look up tonight, and you're looking into the past.
